skills.system_prompt:
You are a professional editor who specialises in making AI-generated text indistinguishable from human writing.

Your task: rewrite the text I give you so it reads as authentic human writing while preserving every factual claim and the original intent.

WHAT TO FIX — detect and rewrite these AI tells:

1. FILLER OPENERS
   Remove: "Certainly!", "Of course!", "Absolutely!", "Great question!", "Sure thing!", "Definitely!", "I'd be happy to..."
   Remove: "I hope this email finds you well", "I hope you're doing well", "Feel free to reach out", "Please don't hesitate to contact me"

2. VAGUE POWER WORDS — replace with specific, concrete language
   Remove: unlock, unleash, leverage, streamline, revolutionise, transform, empower, harness, elevate, amplify, synergise
   Remove: game-changer, groundbreaking, cutting-edge, innovative solution, state-of-the-art, best-in-class, world-class
   Remove: robust, seamlessly, holistically, comprehensively, proactively

3. CORPORATE PADDING — delete entirely
   Remove: "It's worth noting that...", "It goes without saying...", "Needless to say...", "It is important to note..."
   Remove: "Moving forward", "Going forward", "At the end of the day", "In today's [adjective] world..."
   Remove: "The biggest takeaway is...", "It is what it is"

4. STRUCTURAL TELLS
   - If every section has a bullet list, convert some to prose
   - Delete summary paragraphs that repeat what was just said
   - Remove "In conclusion" sections unless the piece genuinely needs one
   - Remove "I hope this helps!" and similar sign-off filler

5. DIVE / DELVE CLICHÉS
   Remove: dive deep, delve into, embark on, explore the nuances, unpack, breakdown, dissect

6. OVER-HEDGING — one qualifier is enough
   Simplify triple qualifications and excessive hedging language

STYLE RULES:
- Preserve ALL factual content — never change meaning
- Keep technical terms that have no cleaner alternative
- Vary sentence length — short punchy sentences work alongside longer ones
- A single sentence can stand alone as its own paragraph for emphasis
- Active voice preferred, but don't force it unnaturally

VOICE STYLE:
[Add your voice notes here]

When finished, output ONLY the rewritten text. No commentary. No explanation. Just the clean output.

examples.label: Email opener
examples.before: I hope this email finds you well! I wanted to reach out to discuss a potential opportunity that I believe could be a game-changer for your business. Our cutting-edge solution seamlessly integrates with your existing workflow to unlock significant value.
examples.after: Quick one — we built something that might save your ops team about four hours a week. It plugs into the tools you're already using. Worth a 20-minute call?

examples.label: Blog intro
examples.before: In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, businesses must leverage cutting-edge AI tools to remain competitive. It's worth noting that the biggest takeaway from recent research is that organisations that fail to adapt risk being left behind.
examples.after: Most companies using AI are still running it like a fancy search engine. The ones pulling ahead are doing something different — they're building reusable skills that compound. Here's what that looks like.

skills.title: Prompt Chaining for Complex Tasks
skills.outcome: Breaks any complex AI task into auditable sequential steps
skills.why: Most prompts fail because you're asking one model to do too much in one shot.
skills.desc: Break multi-step problems into sequential prompts where each output feeds the next input. Reduces hallucinations, keeps LLMs on-task across long workflows, and makes outputs auditable at every step.

cost_estimate.label: Variable
cost_estimate.note: Use model routing to cut chain costs by 60–80%.

recommended_models.best_for: Orchestrator step — best at following JSON contracts
Worker steps — fast, cheap, reliable for simple tasks
Classification and routing steps

not_recommended: Single large models for all steps (expensive, slower)
Models without reliable JSON output for extraction steps

skills.why: Stateless agents forget everything. Add memory and they become genuinely useful.

cost_estimate.label: Moderate

recommended_models.best_for: Best reasoning for memory retrieval decisions
Strong for multi-session summarization

not_recommended: Flash models for memory orchestration (too prone to retrieval errors)
Stateless chat interfaces without system prompt persistence

skills.title: RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
skills.outcome: Connects any AI to your own documents without fine-tuning
skills.why: LLMs don't know your documents. RAG fixes that without fine-tuning or retraining.
skills.desc: Connect any LLM to your own knowledge base using vector search. Answer questions grounded in your specific data — PDFs, wikis, codebases, customer records — with citations and minimal hallucination.

cost_estimate.label: Moderate
cost_estimate.note: Embedding cost is one-time. Query cost scales with document chunk size.

recommended_models.best_for: Best grounding — stays within retrieved context
Cost-effective for high-volume RAG queries

not_recommended: Models without strong instruction following (hallucinate outside retrieved context)
Very large context windows for small document sets (wastes tokens)

cost_estimate.label: Cheap (saves money)

recommended_models.best_for: Router decision layer — near-zero cost

cost_estimate.label: One-time Setup
cost_estimate.note: A well-designed system prompt actually reduces token waste from re-prompting.

cost_estimate.label: One-time Setup

recommended_models.best_for: Best constitutional AI alignment for refusals

skills.title: Few-Shot Prompting
skills.outcome: Locks exact output format and tone with 2–5 examples
skills.why: When you can't fully describe what you want in words, show the model.
skills.desc: Include 2–5 worked examples directly in your prompt and the model infers format, tone, and edge-case handling from them. No fine-tuning required. The fastest way to lock in exact output schemas.

cost_estimate.label: Cheap
cost_estimate.note: Fewer examples = cheaper. 3 high-quality examples beat 10 mediocre ones.

recommended_models.best_for: Works universally — even small models improve with examples

cost_estimate.label: Cheap

Strong reasoning for structured problems
